description:
The TRANSPILER's module resolver ignores `.pmc` while perl and PCL's own loader
prefer it: `Pl::Parser::_find_module_file` probes `-f "$inc/$file"` for a
`.pm` and nothing else, so a directory holding `Foo.pmc` and no `Foo.pm`
resolves for the RUN (`p-find-module-in-inc` / `%p-inc-dir-file` prefer the
`.pmc`, as perl's `require` does) but NOT for the transpile that supplies the
parse facts.

FOUND s490a (Opus), while building #1860's R1/R2 clauses: the two questions
"what will PCL load from this directory" and "what would a child pl2cl resolve
here" gave different answers for a `.pmc`, and a cache clause built on the
former would have invalidated an entry that the re-transpile then rebuilds
identically -- an endless re-transpile.  `%p-inc-dir-file` therefore gained a
`:pmc nil` form with exactly one caller (`%p-dir-holds-p`), and the divergence
itself is filed here rather than papered over.

WHAT DIVERGES, and why it was not fixed in that batch:

  * perl: `require Foo` prefers `Foo.pmc` over `Foo.pm` in the same directory
    (unless $ENV{PERL_DISABLE_PMC}).
  * PCL's RUNTIME agrees (%p-inc-dir-file's PMC clause, and its docstring says
    why: a modern .pmc is alternative SOURCE, which PCL transpiles like a .pm).
  * PCL's TRANSPILER does not: `_find_module_file` builds `Module/Name.pm` and
    stats only that.  So with a `.pmc`-only (or `.pmc`-shadowing) dependency,
    the emission encodes the prototypes and exports of the `.pm` -- or of
    nothing at all, a `missing` record -- while the program LOADS the `.pmc`.

NOT REPRODUCED AGAINST perl HERE: this box has zero `.pmc` files under the
perl 5.40.3 lib tree and PCL's own lib/, so the divergence is latent rather
than measured.  A reproducer is two files in one directory, `B.pm` with
`sub zap ()` and `B.pmc` with `sub zap`, a module A doing `use B; sub go { zap
+ 1 }` -- perl answers 107 (the .pmc, no prototype), PCL should answer 8.
Probe that before fixing, and probe `$INC{'B.pm'}` too: perl records the
requested NAME as the key and the .pmc as the value.

FIX SHAPE (one line, at the ONE resolver): `_find_module_file` prefers
`"$inc/$file" . "c"` when it exists, exactly as `%p-inc-dir-file` does, and
returns that path.  Then the manifest's `dep` path is the `.pmc`, its MD5 is
the `.pmc`'s, and #1860's `:pmc nil` probe can go back to the default -- the
two questions would have one answer again, which is the state rule 11 wants.
Watch the trust class (`trust_class` is path-based, so a `.pmc` under an
installed dir stays `installed`) and `PERL_DISABLE_PMC`, which PCL honours
nowhere today.

Related: #1860 (the resolution clauses, which the `:pmc nil` form serves),
#1284 (one search path), `%p-inc-dir-file`'s docstring.
